newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes lower, seen to drift.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes lower, seen to drift.

text.p: Rubber futures finished easier on Friday in very thin trade with the market seen drifting next week because of a national holiday in Japan and the Christmas Day holiday elsewhere in the region, dealers said.
"I'm just not in the mood to work. Some of my friends are already out attending Christmas parties this afternoon," a local rubber trader said.
Lower Japanese prices depressed local sentiment. Tokyo's benchmark May contract slid 1.3 yen to 146.8 while Kobe's May contract dipped 0.2 yen to 146.3.
The most active month was the April/June TSR20 contract with about 540 tonnes traded, followed by the February RSS3 contract with some 350 tonnes traded, dealers said.
"There was very little buying in the market. People were already in a holiday mood," one trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 125.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.25 cents.

February RSS1 was indicated at 177.50-179.50 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg against 179.50 cents. April/June TSR20 was seen at 174.00-176.00 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.26) a kg from 176.00 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.40) - Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
